title: The night Earth feared a comet's tail ☄️
subject: comet
description:
Would you have bought the pills? 👇

In 1910, Earth was set to pass through the tail of Halley's Comet on May 18/19. After Yerkes Observatory found cyanogen gas in the tail, astronomer Camille Flammarion speculated it could snuff out life. People sealed their homes and sellers offered anti-comet pills, gas masks and umbrellas. The tail was far too thin to matter, and nothing happened. Halley's Comet returns in 2061, and its dust makes the Orionid meteor shower every October.

Sources: Science History Institute, Distillations ("The Comet Panic of 1910 Revisited"), Library of Congress (Chronicling America: Halley's Comet; diagram of Earth's encounter with the tail, May 18/19, 1910), NASA Science (1P/Halley, Orionids)

scenes.text: In 1910, people bought gas masks to survive a comet.
Halley's Comet was back, and on May 18, Earth was set to pass through its glowing tail.
Months earlier, astronomers had found a poisonous gas called cyanogen in that tail.
One famous astronomer even suggested it could snuff out all life.
People sealed their windows, covered keyholes, and bought anti-comet pills.
But the tail was so thin that nothing happened, and Halley's Comet returns in 2061.
